claim: Histone H3 acetylation at K56 and phosphorylation at T45 are two important chromatin modifications that accompany chromatin assembly.
source: Histone H3 acetylation at K56 and phosphorylation at T45 are two important chromatin modifications that accompany chromatin assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about these modifications.

claim: Pkc1 is a key regulator that coordinates the deposition of H3K56 acetylation and H3T45 phosphorylation in S. cerevisiae under conditions of replicative stress.
source: Here we have identified the protein kinase Pkc1 as a key regulator that coordinates the deposition of these modifications in S. cerevisiae under conditions of replicative stress.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: Pkc1 phosphorylates the histone acetyl transferase Rtt109.
source: Pkc1 phosphorylates the histone acetyl transferase Rtt109 and promotes its ability to acetylate H3K56.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Pkc1 phosphorylation of Rtt109 promotes its ability to acetylate H3K56.
source: Pkc1 phosphorylates the histone acetyl transferase Rtt109 and promotes its ability to acetylate H3K56.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing reduced H3K56 acetylation in pkc1 mutants.

claim: Pkc1 enhances H3T45 phosphorylation.
source: Our data also reveal novel cross-talk between two different histone modifications as Pkc1 also enhances H3T45 phosphorylation and this modification is required for H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: H3T45 phosphorylation is required for H3K56 acetylation.
source: Our data also reveal novel cross-talk between two different histone modifications as Pkc1 also enhances H3T45 phosphorylation and this modification is required for H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing reduced H3K56 acetylation in H3(T45A) mutants.

claim: Rtt109-mediated modification of histone H3 by acetylation of lysine 56 (H3K56) is a key event during chromatin reassembly in S. cerevisiae.
source: This process must be tightly controlled and in S. cerevisiae one key event is the Rtt109-mediated modification of histone H3 by acetylation of lysine 56 (H3K56) (Han et al., 2007; Driscoll et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Rtt109 cooperates with two different histone chaperones Asf1 and Vps75.
source: Rtt109 cooperates with two different histone chaperones Asf1 and Vps75 (Tsubota et al., 2007; Driscoll et al., 2007)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Asf1 is the major chaperone involved in promoting H3K56 acetylation.
source: although it is generally accepted that Asf1 is the major chaperone involved in promoting H3K56 acetylation (Keck et al., 2011; Tang et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The signalling pathways controlling Rtt109-mediated H3K56 acetylation are unknown.
source: However, the signalling pathways controlling Rtt109-mediated H3K56 acetylation are unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a knowledge gap.

claim: H3 phosphorylation at threonine T45 (H3T45) occurs coincidentally with DNA replication.
source: Another important modification that occurs coincidentally with DNA replication is H3 phosphorylation at threonine T45 (H3T45)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: H3T45 phosphorylation has no relationship with H3K56 acetylation in the context of an unperturbed cell cycle.
source: but current evidence suggests that this modification has no relationship with the closely located H3K56 acetylation event (Baker et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Cdc7-Dbf4 is a major kinase involved in controlling H3T45 phosphorylation levels in the context of an unperturbed cell cycle.
source: In the context of an unperturbed cell cycle, Cdc7-Dbf4 has been shown to be a major kinase involved in controlling H3T45 phosphorylation levels (Baker et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: S. cerevisiae possesses one protein kinase C isoform, Pkc1.
source: S. cerevisiae possesses one protein kinase C isoform, Pkc1
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Pkc1 plays a major role in cell wall integrity signalling.
source: S. cerevisiae possesses one protein kinase C isoform, Pkc1, and it is known to play a major role in cell wall integrity signalling (reviewed in Levin, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Pkc1 has been implicated in cell cycle events through genetic experiments.
source: Pkc1 has a growing number of nuclear functions and through genetic experiments this protein kinase has previously been implicated in cell cycle events (reviewed in Levin, 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Pkc1 directly affects the cell cycle by inhibiting the activity of the transcriptional coactivator protein Ndd1.
source: However MAP kinase-independent roles for Pkc1 have emerged and Pkc1 was recently shown to directly affect the cell cycle by inhibiting the activity of the transcriptional coactivator protein Ndd1 (Darieva et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: pkc1 mutants are sensitive to hydroxurea (HU) treatment.
source: Indeed, pkc1 mutants are sensitive to hydroxurea (HU) treatment (Queralt and Igual, 2005)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: PKC1 and components of the RSC chromatin remodelling complex are genetically linked.
source: It is unclear how Pkc1 might affect replicative stress but previous genetic studies have linked PKC1 and components of the RSC chromatin remodelling complex and Pkc1 overexpression can suppress the defects associated with RSC mutants (Chai et al., 2005; Hosotani et al., 2001; reviewed in Levin et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Pkc1 overexpression can suppress the defects associated with RSC mutants.
source: It is unclear how Pkc1 might affect replicative stress but previous genetic studies have linked PKC1 and components of the RSC chromatin remodelling complex and Pkc1 overexpression can suppress the defects associated with RSC mutants (Chai et al., 2005; Hosotani et al., 2001; reviewed in Levin et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Temperature sensitive pkc1-14 cells grown at 34°C to inactivate Pkc1 were inviable in comparison to cells containing wild-type PKC1.
source: In comparison to cells containing wild-type PKC1 (DK186), temperature sensitive pkc1-14 (DK1690) cells, grown at 34ºC to inactivate Pkc1 were inviable (Figure 1A, top panel)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The presence of sorbitol saved the pkc1-14 mutant phenotype.
source: The presence of sorbitol saved the pkc1-14 mutant phenotype (Figure 1A, middle panel)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: HU sensitivity was observed in pkc1-14 cells in the presence of sorbitol.
source: The presence of sorbitol saved the pkc1-14 mutant phenotype (Figure 1A, middle panel) but HU sensitivity was observed under these conditions (Figure 1A, bottom panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: bck1Δ cells were not sensitive to HU.
source: Indeed bck1Δ (Y01328) cells were not sensitive to HU, further emphasising a new alternative mechanism of action for Pkc1 under replicative stress conditions (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Wild-type Pkc1 was able to rescue the growth defect of pkc1-14 cells in the presence of HU.
source: However, while wild-type (WT) Pkc1 was able to rescue the growth defect of pkc1-14 cells, the catalytically dead version was unable to do so (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Catalytically dead Pkc1 was unable to rescue the growth defect of pkc1-14 cells in the presence of HU.
source: However, while wild-type (WT) Pkc1 was able to rescue the growth defect of pkc1-14 cells, the catalytically dead version was unable to do so (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Pkc1 kinase activity is required for protecting cells from replicative stress.
source: Together, these experiments demonstrate that Pkc1 kinase activity is required for protecting cells from replicative stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Acetylation of histone H3 at lysine 56 (H3K56) during S phase is an important modification in ensuring the correct assembly of newly synthesised nucleosomes and their incorporation into chromatin.
source: During S phase, acetylation of histone H3 at lysine 56 (H3K56) is an important modification in ensuring the correct assembly of newly synthesised nucleosomes and their incorporation into chromatin (Li et al., 2008; Masumoto et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: Wild-type cells showed accumulation of acetylated H3K56 upon release from a HU block.
source: Upon release from a HU block, wild-type cells showed accumulation of acetylated H3K56 (Figure 2A, lanes 1–6).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Temperature sensitive pkc1-21 cells showed much reduced levels of H3K56 acetylation when grown at 34°C upon release from a HU block.
source: In contrast, temperature sensitive pkc1-21 cells (DK1697) showed much reduced levels of H3K56 acetylation when grown at 34ºC (Figure 2A, lanes 7–12)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: pkc1-21 cells progressed through S phase and arrested at G2 despite reduced H3K56 acetylation.
source: In contrast, temperature sensitive pkc1-21 cells (DK1697) showed much reduced levels of H3K56 acetylation when grown at 34ºC (Figure 2A, lanes 7–12) even though they had progressed through S phase and arrested at G2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Reduced H3K56 acetylation was also observed in pkc1-14 cells upon release from a HU block.
source: Importantly, this effect was not limited to strains harbouring the pkc1-21 allele but was also observed in a different temperature sensitive strain, harbouring the pkc1-14 allele either upon release from a HU block (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Reduced H3K56 acetylation was observed in pkc1-14 cells upon entry into S phase upon release from an α factor block.
source: Importantly, this effect was not limited to strains harbouring the pkc1-21 allele but was also observed in a different temperature sensitive strain, harbouring the pkc1-14 allele either upon release from a HU block (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) or upon entry into S phase upon release from an α factor block (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Rtt109 acetylates histone H3 at lysine 9 (H3K9).
source: H3K56 acetylation is deposited by Rtt109, and this enzyme also acetylates histone H3 at lysine 9 (H3K9) (Driscoll et al., 2007; Han et al., 2007; Tsubota et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results with supporting citations.

claim: pkc1-14 cells showed much reduced levels of H3K9 acetylation.
source: Interestingly, in addition to H3K56 acetylation defects, pkc1-14 cells showed much reduced levels of H3K9 acetylation (Figure 2B, middle panel)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Reduced H3K9 acetylation in pkc1-14 cells suggests a defect in Rtt109 activity.
source: Interestingly, in addition to H3K56 acetylation defects, pkc1-14 cells showed much reduced levels of H3K9 acetylation (Figure 2B, middle panel) which suggests a defect in Rtt109 activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of reduced H3K9 acetylation.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of Pkc1 activity with cercosporamide reduced H3K56 acetylation following release from a HU block.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of Pkc1 activity reduced H3K56 acetylation but importantly did not affect another histone H3 acetylation event at lysine 18 (H3K18) (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of Pkc1 activity with cercosporamide did not affect H3K18 acetylation.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of Pkc1 activity reduced H3K56 acetylation but importantly did not affect another histone H3 acetylation event at lysine 18 (H3K18) (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The effect of cercosporamide on H3K56 acetylation was through Pkc1.
source: We also examined whether combinatorial genetic inactivation and pharmacological inhibition of Pkc1 has additive effects but none were observed, indicating that the effect of cercosporamide was through Pkc1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Loss of Pkc1 in temperature sensitive strains resulted in stronger reductions in H3K56ac levels than following cercosporamide treatment.
source: We note however that the loss of Pkc1 in the temperature sensitive strains resulted in stronger reductions in H3K56ac levels than following cercosporamide treatment, most likely due to incomplete Pkc1 inhibition in the latter case.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an observation with a proposed explanation.

claim: Pkc1 plays an important role in promoting H3K56 acetylation under replicative stress conditions.
source: Together these results demonstrate an important role for Pkc1 in promoting H3K56 acetylation under replicative stress conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in Figure 2.

claim: Rtt109 has a potential phosphorylation site at threonine 46 (T46) which partially matches the PKC consensus sequence.
source: Inspection of Rtt109 sequence revealed a potential phosphorylation site at threonine 46 (T46) which partially matches the PKC consensus sequence (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A phospho-specific antibody specifically recognised a phosphorylated peptide surrounding T46 of Rtt109.
source: To establish whether Rtt109 can be phosphorylated by Pkc1 at this site, we raised a phospho-specific antibody which specifically recognised a phosphorylated peptide surrounding T46 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Pkc1 was able to phosphorylate Rtt109 in the context of a purified recombinant Rtt109-Vps75 heterodimer in vitro.
source: In vitro kinase assays revealed that Pkc1 was able to phosphorylate Rtt109 in the context of a purified recombinant Rtt109-Vps75 heterodimer (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Rtt109 phosphorylation by Pkc1 was reduced to background levels following treatment with lambda phosphatase.
source: This phosphorylation was reduced to background levels following treatment with lambda phosphatase (Figure 3B, lane 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Pkc1 and Rtt109 could interact in vitro.
source: Immunoprecipitation assays demonstrated that Pkc1 and Rtt109 could interact in vitro (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Rtt109 T46 became strongly phosphorylated in vivo following HU treatment.
source: Rtt109 phosphorylation at T46 could also be identified in vivo following HU treatment (Figure 3C, lanes 1–4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Rtt109 T46 phosphorylation was subsequently lost upon release from HU arrest.
source: This phosphorylation was subsequently lost upon release from HU arrest (Figure 3C, lanes 5–6).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Treatment of cells with cercosporamide prior to HU addition blocked the appearance of Rtt109 phosphorylation at T46.
source: Importantly, treatment of cells with cercosporamide prior to HU addition blocked the appearance of Rtt109 phosphorylation at T46 (Figure 3D)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Pkc1 plays a role in promoting Rtt109 phosphorylation under replicative stress conditions.
source: Importantly, treatment of cells with cercosporamide prior to HU addition blocked the appearance of Rtt109 phosphorylation at T46 (Figure 3D), demonstrating a role for Pkc1 in promoting Rtt109 phosphorylation under replicative stress conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cercosporamide experiment.

claim: In cells undergoing replicative stress, Rtt109 is phosphorylated in a Pkc1-dependent manner, most likely through direct phosphorylation by Pkc1.
source: These data therefore indicate that in cells undergoing replicative stress, Rtt109 is phosphorylated in a Pkc1-dependent manner, most likely through direct phosphorylation by Pkc1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Rtt109 phosphorylation.

claim: rtt109Δ cells grew poorly in the presence of HU.
source: In the presence of HU, rtt109Δ cells grew poorly (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The growth defect of rtt109Δ cells in HU could be rescued by re-expressing wild-type Rtt109.
source: This growth defect could be rescued by re-expressing wild-type Rtt109 but this rescue was lost with the non-phosphorylatable Rtt109(T46A) mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The rescue of rtt109Δ growth defect in HU was lost with the non-phosphorylatable Rtt109(T46A) mutant.
source: This growth defect could be rescued by re-expressing wild-type Rtt109 but this rescue was lost with the non-phosphorylatable Rtt109(T46A) mutant.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Rtt109(T46D) was able to suppress the growth defect of rtt109Δ cells in HU.
source: In contrast, Rtt109(T46D) was able to suppress the growth defect (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The insertion of a phosphomimetic residue at the Pkc1 phosphorylation site reinstated the activity of Rtt109.
source: In contrast, Rtt109(T46D) was able to suppress the growth defect (Figure 4A) indicating that the insertion of a phosphomimetic residue at the Pkc1 phosphorylation site reinstated the activity of Rtt109.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the rescue experiment with Rtt109(T46D).

claim: H3K56 acetylation was severely depleted in rtt109Δ cells.
source: As expected, this was severely depleted in rtt109Δ cells but restored upon re-expression of wild-type Rtt109 (Figure 4B, left panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: H3K56 acetylation was restored in rtt109Δ cells upon re-expression of wild-type Rtt109.
source: As expected, this was severely depleted in rtt109Δ cells but restored upon re-expression of wild-type Rtt109 (Figure 4B, left panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Rtt109(T46A) only partially re-constituted H3K56 acetylation levels and the kinetics were delayed.
source: Rtt109(T46A) only partially re-constituted H3K56 acetylation levels and the kinetics were delayed whereas Rtt109(T46D) promoted rapid and high levels of H3K56 acetylation (Figure 4B, left panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Rtt109(T46D) promoted rapid and high levels of H3K56 acetylation.
source: Rtt109(T46A) only partially re-constituted H3K56 acetylation levels and the kinetics were delayed whereas Rtt109(T46D) promoted rapid and high levels of H3K56 acetylation (Figure 4B, left panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Pkc1-mediated phosphorylation of Rtt109 is required for its ability to promote H3K56 acetylation.
source: These results are fully consistent with a role for Pkc1-mediated phosphorylation of Rtt109 being required for its ability to promote H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Rtt109 mutant experiments.

claim: Wild-type Rtt109 was inducibly expressed to high levels upon release from HU arrest.
source: Interestingly, we found that while wild-type Rtt109 and Rtt109(T46D) were inducibly expressed to high levels upon release from HU arrest, Rtt109(T46A) expression was delayed and reached a lower level (Figure 4B, right hand panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Rtt109(T46D) was inducibly expressed to high levels upon release from HU arrest.
source: Interestingly, we found that while wild-type Rtt109 and Rtt109(T46D) were inducibly expressed to high levels upon release from HU arrest, Rtt109(T46A) expression was delayed and reached a lower level (Figure 4B, right hand panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Rtt109(T46A) expression was delayed and reached a lower level upon release from HU arrest.
source: Interestingly, we found that while wild-type Rtt109 and Rtt109(T46D) were inducibly expressed to high levels upon release from HU arrest, Rtt109(T46A) expression was delayed and reached a lower level (Figure 4B, right hand panels).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Pkc1-mediated phosphorylation might be important for stabilising Rtt109.
source: This suggested that Pkc1-mediated phosphorylation might be important for stabilising Rtt109.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of differential Rtt109 protein levels.

claim: Rtt109 protein was expressed to lower levels in pkc1-14 cells.
source: Indeed, we found that Rtt109 protein was expressed to lower levels in pkc1-14 cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Lower Rtt109 protein levels in pkc1-14 cells were not due to a transcriptional defect.
source: This was not due to a transcriptional defect as RTT109 mRNA levels were elevated in pkc1-14 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: pkc1-14 cells are attempting to compensate for the loss in Rtt109 protein by elevating RTT109 mRNA levels.
source: This was not due to a transcriptional defect as RTT109 mRNA levels were elevated in pkc1-14 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that these cells are attempting to compensate for the loss in Rtt109 protein.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of elevated mRNA but lower protein levels.

claim: Lower level of Rtt109 likely contributes to the decreased levels of H3K56 acetylation in pkc1-14 cells.
source: This lower level of Rtt109 likely contributes to the decreased levels of H3K56 acetylation we observed.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation of lower Rtt109 protein levels.

claim: Pkc1-mediated Rtt109 phosphorylation is required for maintaining Rtt109 protein levels and H3K56 acetylation levels as cells recover from HU-mediated replicative stress.
source: Together, these results indicated that Pkc1-mediated Rtt109 phosphorylation is required for maintaining Rtt109 protein levels and H3K56 acetylation levels as cells recover from HU-mediated replicative stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on Rtt109 phosphorylation and protein levels.

claim: A highly significant overlap was observed for pkc1-14 cells or cells expressing Rtt109(T46A) in genes either downregulated or upregulated compared to wild-type cells released from HU block.
source: Indeed, in cells released from HU block, a highly significant overlap was observed for pkc1-14 cells or cells expressing Rtt109(T46A) in genes either downregulated or upregulated compared to wild-type cells (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: No significant overlaps were observed when genes regulated in opposite directions in pkc1-14 and Rtt109(T46A) mutant strains were considered.
source: Importantly no such significant overlaps were observed when we considered genes that were regulated in opposite directions in the two mutant strains (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: There was a strong overlap in gene ontology (GO) terms between pkc1-14 and Rtt109(T46A) mutant strains.
source: Furthermore, when we considered the biological processes that were affected, there was a strong overlap in gene ontology (GO) terms, with over-representation of GO terms associated with processes such as 'cell wall' and 'nucleolus' strongly associated with both mutant strains and reciprocal effects seen with 'telomere maintenance' and 'DNA helicase activity' (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: GO terms associated with 'cell wall' and 'nucleolus' were strongly associated with both pkc1-14 and Rtt109(T46A) mutant strains.
source: Furthermore, when we considered the biological processes that were affected, there was a strong overlap in gene ontology (GO) terms, with over-representation of GO terms associated with processes such as 'cell wall' and 'nucleolus' strongly associated with both mutant strains and reciprocal effects seen with 'telomere maintenance' and 'DNA helicase activity' (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Reciprocal effects were seen with 'telomere maintenance' and 'DNA helicase activity' GO terms in pkc1-14 and Rtt109(T46A) mutant strains.
source: Furthermore, when we considered the biological processes that were affected, there was a strong overlap in gene ontology (GO) terms, with over-representation of GO terms associated with processes such as 'cell wall' and 'nucleolus' strongly associated with both mutant strains and reciprocal effects seen with 'telomere maintenance' and 'DNA helicase activity' (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: No rescue of the growth defects of pkc1-14 cells in the presence of HU was observed with the phosphomimetic version of Rtt109.
source: One prediction of these results is that the phosphomimetic version of Rtt109 might be able to bypass the defects seen in pkc1-14 cells. However, no rescue of the growth defects of pkc1-14 cells in the presence of HU was observed (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pkc1 has a direct role in controlling H3K56 acetylation through Rtt109 phosphorylation but also controls additional activities.
source: Therefore a working model suggested a direct role for Pkc1 in controlling H3K56 acetylation through Rtt109 phosphorylation but also that additional activities were controlled by Pkc1 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data.

claim: PKCδ phosphorylates histone H3 at threonine 45 (H3T45) in mammalian cells.
source: Previous results in mammalian cells had shown that PKCδ phosphorylates histone H3 at threonine 45 (H3T45) (Hurd et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a supporting citation.

claim: H3T45 is conserved in S. cerevisiae.
source: As this residue is conserved in S. cerevisiae (Figure 6A)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Pkc1 could phosphorylate H3T45 in vitro using purified histone H3 and immunoprecipitated Pkc1.
source: We therefore examined whether Pkc1 could phosphorylate H3T45 in vitro by using purified histone H3 and immunoprecipitated Pkc1p. Efficient H3 phosphorylation was observed (Figure 6B)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Phosphorylation at T45 was confirmed as the only major phosphorylation site by mass spectrometry.
source: and phosphorylation at T45 was confirmed as the only major phosphorylation site by mass spectrometry (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: H3T45 became strongly phosphorylated in wild-type cells as they were released from a HU-mediated block.
source: As cells were released from a HU-mediated block, H3T45 became strongly phosphorylated in wild-type cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: No rises in H3T45 phosphorylation were observed upon ablation of Pkc1 activity in pkc1-14 cells.
source: However, no such rises in H3T45 phosphorylation were observed upon ablation of Pkc1 activity in pkc1-14 cells (Figure 6D, lanes 7–12).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Pkc1 mediates histone H3 phosphorylation under conditions of replicative stress.
source: The results therefore indicate that Pkc1 mediates histone H3 phosphorylation under conditions of replicative stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on H3T45 phosphorylation.

claim: H3K56 acetylation was greatly reduced in cells containing the H3(T45A) allele upon release from a HU block.
source: Importantly, H3K56 acetylation was greatly reduced in cells containing the H3(T45A) allele upon release from a HU block (Figure 7A, lanes 3 and 4; Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: Only a small change in H3K56 acetylation was observed in H3(T45A) cells upon release from an alpha factor block under normal growth conditions.
source: In contrast only a small change in H3K56 acetylation was observed upon release from an alpha factor block under normal growth conditions (Figure 7A, lanes 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: H3K56 acetylation accumulated following HU removal in wild-type cells released from an alpha factor-mediated G1 arrest into HU.
source: However, if cells were released from an alpha factor-mediated G1 arrest into HU, and the HU subsequently removed, H3K56 acetylation again accumulated following HU removal in wild-type cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results.

claim: H3K56 acetylation did not accumulate in cells harbouring the H3(T45A) mutant allele following HU removal after release from alpha factor into HU.
source: This accumulation of H3K56 acetylation did not occur in cells harbouring the H3(T45A) mutant allele (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: There is functional coupling between H3T45 phosphorylation and H3K56 acetylation.
source: These results suggested functional coupling between H3T45 phosphorylation and H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that H3(T45A) reduces H3K56 acetylation.

claim: Only low levels of H3K56 acetylation were observed in H3(T45A) cells in the presence of Rtt109(T46D).
source: However, only low levels of H3K56 acetylation were observed in the presence of Rtt109(T46D) (Figure 7C)
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Rtt109(T46D) was unable to suppress the defects from H3(T45A).
source: However, only low levels of H3K56 acetylation were observed in the presence of Rtt109(T46D) (Figure 7C), demonstrating that this protein was unable to suppress the defects from H3(T45A)
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the experiment.

claim: H3T45 phosphorylation plays a crucial role in promoting H3K56 acetylation.
source: thereby indicating a crucial role for H3T45 phosphorylation in promoting H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the inability of Rtt109(T46D) to rescue H3(T45A) defects.

claim: Rtt109(T46D) couldn't bypass the growth defects of H3(T45A) cells in HU.
source: Indeed, the Rtt109(T46D) mutant couldn't bypass the growth defects of H3(T45A) cells in HU (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Rtt109(T46D) was unable to rescue the growth defect of H3(K56R) cells in HU.
source: We also tested whether Rtt109(D) could bypass the HU-mediated growth defects of H3(K56R) cells but again this mutant was unable to rescue the growth defect (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Rtt109-mediated H3K56 acetylation is important for protecting against the deleterious effects of HU treatment.
source: This further emphasises the importance of Rtt109-mediated H3K56 acetylation in protecting against the deleterious effects of HU treatment, even when H3T45 was available for phosphorylation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the inability of Rtt109(T46D) to rescue H3(K56R) defects.

claim: Pkc1 signals through promoting phosphorylation of both Rtt109 and histone H3 to promote H3K56 acetylation.
source: These results lead to a model whereby Pkc1 signals through promoting phosphorylation of both Rtt109 and histone H3 to promote H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data.

claim: Pairwise comparisons of gene expression changes between pkc1-14, H3(T45A) and Rtt109(T46A) mutant strains showed highly significant overlaps in genes being upregulated.
source: Indeed pairwise comparisons of the gene expression changes observed between these strains following release from a HU block, showed highly significant overlaps in genes being upregulated in all cases (Figure 7E; Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7E and Figure 5B.

claim: Of the 51 genes showing significant upregulation in the pkc1 and Rtt109(T46A) mutant strains, 41 (80%) were also upregulated in the H3(T45A) mutant strain.
source: Importantly though, of the 51 genes showing significant upregulation in the pkc1 and Rtt109(T46A) mutant strains, 41 (80%) were also upregulated in the H3(T45A) mutant strain (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Consistent co-regulation of genes in the 'DNA helicase' GO term category could be observed across all mutant strains (pkc1-14, H3(T45A), Rtt109(T46A)).
source: Moreover, consistent co-regulation of genes in the 'DNA helicase' GO term category could be observed across all mutant strains (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 7F.

claim: pkc1-14, H3(T45A), and Rtt109(T46A) mutants exhibit common defects in gene expression.
source: These mutants therefore exhibit common defects in gene expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gene expression analysis.

claim: Pkc1 coordinates histone H3 modifications during the replicative stress response.
source: This finding provides further supporting evidence that adds to the mechanistic links we have uncovered between Pkc1, Rtt109, H3T45 phosphorylation and H3K56 acetylation, and strengthens our major discovery that Pkc1 coordinates histone H3 modifications during the replicative stress response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined experimental data.

claim: At least two different kinases are involved in controlling H3T45 phosphorylation, with Cdc7/Dbf4 operating during an unperturbed cell cycle and Pkc1 operating under replicative stress conditions.
source: Here we focussed on histone H3 modification control under replicative stress conditions and in combination with previous results (Baker et al., 2010) our data indicate that at least two different kinases are involved in controlling H3T45 phosphorylation, with Cdc7/Dbf4 operating during an unperturbed cell cycle and Pkc1 operating under replicative stress conditions where it also coordinates H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the current study and previous work.

claim: Pkc1 promotes the re-activation of H3 modifications upon removal of replicative stress.
source: It is not clear how this delay is achieved but Pkc1 promotes the re-activation of H3 modifications upon removal of replicative stress.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Pkc1 controls H3K56 acetylation through phosphorylating the Rtt109 acetyltransferase.
source: Mechanistically, Pkc1 controls H3K56 acetylation through phosphorylating the Rtt109 acetyltransferase.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Pkc1 phosphorylation stabilises Rtt109 and safeguards its availability for modifying histone H3 following removal of replicative stress.
source: This modification stabilises Rtt109 and thus safeguards its availability for modifying histone H3 following removal of replicative stress and re-entry into the cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Under replicative stress conditions, H3T45 phosphorylation is critically important for coupled H3K56 acetylation.
source: Under replicative stress conditions, H3T45 phosphorylation appears to be critically important for coupled H3K56 acetylation, and this phosphorylation event is promoted by Pkc1-mediated H3T45 phosphorylation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Pkc1-mediated H3T45 phosphorylation is likely direct as histone H3 is efficiently phosphorylated at this site in vitro.
source: This is likely direct as histone H3 is efficiently phosphorylated at this site in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the in vitro kinase assay.

claim: Pkc1 promotes the coordinate modification of H3T45 phosphorylation and H3K56 acetylation, with H3T45 phosphorylation being functionally coupled to H3K56 acetylation.
source: This leads to a model (Figure 7G) whereby Pkc1 promotes the coordinate modification of these two chromatin modifications and H3T45 phosphorylation is functionally coupled to H3K56 acetylation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a model based on the study findings.

claim: One outcome of perturbed Pkc1 activity and its downstream molecular events following HU treatment is likely to be defective chromatin assembly.
source: One outcome of perturbed Pkc1 activity and its downstream molecular events following HU treatment is likely to be defective chromatin assembly and preliminary evidence suggest that this might be the case (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation with preliminary supporting data.

claim: pkc1, rtt109(T46A) and H3(T45A) mutants show consistent sensitivity to HU treatment.
source: Our data show a consistent sensitivity of pkc1, rtt109(T46A) and H3(T45A) mutants to HU treatment
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the findings.

claim: H3(K56A) alleles are sensitive to HU.
source: which complements previous data showing that H3(K56A) alleles are also sensitive to HU (Matsubara et al., 2007)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The H3(T45A) strain is sensitive to both MMS and 6-AU.
source: For example, the H3(T45A) strain is sensitive to both MMS and 6-AU whereas the rtt109(T46A) strain is only sensitive to MMS (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on unpublished data.

claim: The rtt109(T46A) strain is only sensitive to MMS.
source: For example, the H3(T45A) strain is sensitive to both MMS and 6-AU whereas the rtt109(T46A) strain is only sensitive to MMS (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion based on unpublished data.

claim: TORC2 has been shown to phosphorylate and activate Pkc1.
source: Alternatively, other upstream pathways might be involved, and one potential link might be through TOR signalling as TORC2 has been shown to phosphorylate and activate Pkc1 (Nomura and Inoue, 2015)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: TOR signalling has been linked to H3K56 acetylation.
source: and TOR signalling has also been linked to H3K56 acetylation (Chen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: PKCδ has been shown to phosphorylate H3T45 under apoptotic conditions in mammals.
source: Our work may be directly relevant to mammalian systems where PKCδ has been shown to phosphorylate H3T45 under apoptotic conditions (Hurd et al., 2009)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: AKT has been identified as an additional H3T45 kinase under DNA damage conditions in mammals.
source: although others have identified AKT as an additional H3T45 kinase under DNA damage conditions (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: H3K56 acetylation is induced by replicative stress in mammals.
source: It is not clear whether PKC is linked to H3K56 acetylation in mammals but this modification is induced by replicative stress and its deposition is mediated by p300/CBP, the functional homologue of Rtt109 (Das et al., 2009; Vempati et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: p300/CBP is the functional homologue of Rtt109 in mammals.
source: It is not clear whether PKC is linked to H3K56 acetylation in mammals but this modification is induced by replicative stress and its deposition is mediated by p300/CBP, the functional homologue of Rtt109 (Das et al., 2009; Vempati et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: Atypical protein kinase C zeta has been shown to phosphorylate and control the histone acetylation output of CBP in the context of neuronal differentiation.
source: Indeed, atypical protein kinase C zeta has been shown to phosphorylate and control the histone acetylation output of CBP in the context of neuronal differentiation (Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Oncogene-driven replicative stress is an important contributory event in human cancer.
source: Given these links between PKC and CBP/p300 it appears likely that our findings will be directly relevant to human cancer where oncogene-driven replicative stress is an important contributory event (Bartek et al., 2007)
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.
